div.div:
When the player enters the dungeon, they arrive at the hub.
Pillar
To go into a dungeon
one
pillar needs to be activated.
Each pillar has a
buff
and a
debuff
, as well as (optionally) an item requirement.
For Example:
Enemies deal twice as much damage
Dungeons drop twice as much loot
Bow required
The following dungeon will have said buffs and debuffs. Sometimes, a item will be required. The dungeon then will be "item aware" (see below).
Powering up a pillar also requires energy, thus limiting how often you can activate the portal (see player).
Big Boss Door
In this hub there also is a big omounous boss door.
Opening it, will lead to a big boss battle. Potentially offering high rewards, but also high risk of dieing.
The door has a certain amount (currently: 4?) of locks.
Upon defeating a mini boss inside a dungeon (and thus "completing" the dungeon), one lock will disappear.
Not every dungeon run may lead to a mini boss being defeated (for various reasons), but on average it should take around 4-6 dungeon runs to open this door.
Loot also needs to be offered. You can't just activate all locks, go out, save your loot, go back and fight it with no risks attached.

div.div:
The Player can acquire multiple "items" throughout playing the game.
Said items have some story relevance and may have to be found inside dungeons. Possibly as schematics, then find parts to build it and finally get the item and upgrade it.
Items are Zelda-like. Meaning: Every item has a purpose to exist.
For example, a bow can be used to damage enemies and bosses, but also shoot things like a trigger for a door from afar.
As another example, a bomb can be used to explode near enemies, but also to break open designated wall sections.
Dungeons can also become "item-aware" (see: Dungeons).

display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: rgb(255, 255, 255); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: none; white-space: normal; overflow-wrap: normal;
div.p:
Upon entering a dungeon, a random location will be picked for the portal. The player will enter the dungeon through this portal from the hub. T
he player should be exploring, fighting enemies, and especially: collecting loot! Lots of loot.

To progress through the dungeon, the player will need to solve a bunch of puzzles. Some puzzles will be simpler than others, some doors also will simply open if you defeat every enemy in the room, others require a key, some are actual puzzles, etc.
But be careful! Dieing will throw you out of the dungeon and major parts of your loot will be lost (based on portal stability).

Each dungeon will also spawn a mini-boss.
If the boss gets defeated, one of the locks on the big boss door in the hub will be unlocked and the current combination of buffs, debuffs and items will be added to the big boss.
(See: Big Boss)
Said mini-boss must be defeated to open the portal again so the player can get back to the hub with all their loot.
Alternatively, the player can choose to spend their energy (see Player -> Energy Meter) to open the portal again.
The more energy you put into the portal, the more stable it will become. The more stable = The more loot can be kept.
Defeating the mini-boss will result in a fully stable portal.

Some areas of the dungeon will be unreachable.
And this is by design! We are exploring some ancient ruins, some places simply won't be visitable.
Loot, puzzles and even the mini-boss can spawn in those rooms ... so if bad luck strikes, you'll find the mini-boss sitting on the biggest pile of loot you've seen in a room you will never be able to access! And to make it worse: You are all out of energy so you can't even stabilize the portal ... R.I.P.
div.div:
Item Augmentation:
A dungeon can be item-augmented (see: Hub). Puzzles and enemies then will be able to utilize said item and integrate it into their design. Not everything will be augmented, it will be a mix between "normal" puzzles/enemies and "item-augmented" puzzles/enemies. The mini-boss and puzzles will
require
the item to be used, but enemies can be killed normally for the most part (just very VERY slowly).

div.div:
Player has an energy source.
Something like a "battery".
The battery will be used for various mechanics, such as:
- Powering up pillars to activate the dungeon portal
- Using items
The battery will have a tiny capacity at the beginning and can barely power anything. Overtime, this should be upgradable.
Going out of the dungeon (outside of hub!) will recharge the battery.
Possibly... solar powered?

div.div:
The big boss should consist of different parts.
It could be a kind of machine or something.
Each part of the boss can be of different types,
but is mainly dedicted by what locks the door
was opened with. So for example one dungeon
was bow-augmented, then one part of the boss
will be "bow-aware". Meaning, you will need to
kill the boss
with the bow
. ... or at least parts
of them. Furthermore, the boss may do
mechanics which can only be prevented with
the item-augmentation.
This should create a challenging boss fight
where you will need to do mechanics, while
fighting the boss and doing damage.
But, taking damage will be a big problem as
dieing will throw you out with major loot loss.
(Note: Loot loss could be based on boss HP.
If you die at 5% Boss HP then most of your loot
will still be saved!)

div.div:
Buff/Debuff mechanic:
During the boss fight, any buffs and debuffs picked up during the dungeon runs will also be applied to the big boss.
Possibly, buffed.
Say your augmentations durign the dungeons where:
- More loot / Enemies deal more damage
- More HP / Enemies have more HP (+ Bow)
- More loot / More Enemies (+ Bombs)
- Attack damage increase / Enemies hit harder
Then the big boss will be doing more damage, has more HP, spawns more adds and will hit harder. Additionally, the boss will require you to use bombs and your bow to avoid mechanics.
On the other hand, you will get more loot (twice actually! Buffs stack!), you will have more HP and do more damage.
Additionally, energy (see: Player -> Energy charge) can be used to block out augmentations at the risk of having less energy to spend ... (Note: Up to 2?)

div.div:
Your house will also be a shop (like in Moonlighter as an example).
To get money, you want to sell loot.
To get loot, you want to go into dungeons.
Items can be sold at any price, but customers will only buy items if the market value (made up ofc ...) is within the range of expectation, or, they really desire the item.
However, you will also need this loot to upgrade your items, weapons, build stuff, etc.
